sections.markdown:
## C — Restrictions and endorsements: where they print, vision restrictions, special-needs restrictions, endorsement and restriction codes, the motorcycle learner's permit and endorsement, autocycles, motor driven cycles (MDC) and the for-hire endorsement
Knowledge domain: the letters and numbers that can appear on an Indiana credential and the vehicles they unlock — vision and special-needs restrictions, the restriction and endorsement code chart, the motorcycle learner's permit and endorsement, autocycles, motor driven cycles and the for-hire endorsement. Motorcycle and for-hire items are kept for completeness and marked as such in C2.

FACT_ID: sec03-F01 | anchor: A01
Restrictions and endorsements appear in the lower left corner of an Indiana credential, and their meanings are printed on the back of the card. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec03-F02 | anchor: A01
Vision screening results are the most common source of restrictions on learner's permits and driver's licenses. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec03-F03 | anchor: A01
Restriction B means the driver must wear glasses or contact lenses when driving. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec03-F04 | anchor: A01
Restriction F means the vehicle must have outside mirrors or a rearview camera whenever the holder drives. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec03-F05 | anchor: A01
Restriction G limits the holder to driving in daylight only. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec03-F06 | anchor: A01
BMV examiners decide whether a person whose disability affects normal operation of a standard vehicle gets a restricted license, which may require specific equipment or other accommodations. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec03-F07 | anchor: A01
On a base driver's license, endorsement L stands for motorcycle and endorsement 2 for for-hire, while on an ID card endorsement B stands for motor driven cycle. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec03-F08 | anchor: A01
Base license restriction codes include C for a mechanical aid or adaptive device, D for a prosthetic aid, J for specific limitations, 6 for an interlock device and 8 for a medical condition. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec03-F09 | anchor: A01
Codes 3 (photo exempt), 7 (seat belt exempt) and 9 (lawful temporary resident) appear as restrictions on both base licenses and ID cards. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec03-F10 | anchor: A01
Restriction H limits motorcycle riding to a three-wheel bike, S to a motorcycle with a sidecar, 2 marks an HTV conditional license and 5 means the holder may drive only under specific conditions. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec03-F11 | anchor: A02
A motorcycle learner's permit requires a valid Indiana driver's license and a passed knowledge exam based on the Motorcycle Operator's Manual. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec03-F12 | anchor: A02
A motorcycle permit holder must wear a helmet, may not carry passengers, and may ride only in the daylight window that the manual bounds by one-half hour before sunrise and one-half hour after sunset. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec03-F13 | anchor: A02
A motorcycle learner's permit is valid for one year and can be issued or renewed no more than three times in a five-year period. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec03-F14 | anchor: A02
If the endorsement is not earned before the renewed motorcycle permit expires, the rider must wait one year for a new permit or complete a Ride Safe Indiana safety course. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec03-F15 | anchor: A02
A first-time license applicant aged 16 or older who has completed a motorcycle safety course can receive the motorcycle endorsement together with the new license. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec03-F16 | anchor: A02
A motorcycle endorsement requires, at any age, either a completed Ride Safe Indiana safety course or passing both the motorcycle knowledge exam and the riding skills exam. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec03-F17 | anchor: A02
A new resident holding a valid motorcycle endorsement or motorcycle license from another state adds the Indiana endorsement after passing only the motorcycle knowledge exam. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec03-F18 | anchor: A02
A motorcycle endorsement lasts as long as the driver's license, the license can be renewed with it up to two years early at a branch or online, and an unexpired endorsement carries no extra fee at renewal. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec03-F19 | anchor: A03
An autocycle is a three-wheeled vehicle with a fully or partly enclosed seating area, a roll cage or roll hoops, a safety belt for each occupant, anti-lock brakes and steering wheel and pedal controls. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec03-F20 | anchor: A03
A valid Indiana driver's license is enough to drive an autocycle; no motorcycle permit or endorsement is needed. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec03-F21 | anchor: A03
An autocycle must be driven from a seat, without carrying a package in hand, and the manual bars operating more than one autocycle in a single traffic lane. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec03-F22 | anchor: A03
Everyone in an autocycle must wear a seat belt, and an autocycle cannot be used for a driver's license skills exam. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec03-F23 | anchor: A03
A motor driven cycle has a seat or saddle, runs on no more than three wheels, meets state and federal equipment rules, has an engine of 50 cubic centimeters or less and is registered as an MDC. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec03-F24 | anchor: A03
An MDC endorsement is added to an ID card at its next issuance after the holder passes the MDC knowledge exam, and holders of a valid permit or license need no MDC endorsement. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec03-F25 | anchor: A03
An MDC rider must be at least 15, and riders under 18 must wear a helmet plus protective glasses, goggles or a transparent face shield. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec03-F26 | anchor: A03
An MDC must be ridden astride the seat with headlamps on and without carrying a package in hand. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec03-F27 | anchor: A03
An MDC must stay near the right edge of the road except when passing or preparing to turn left, and may go no faster than 35 miles per hour. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec03-F28 | anchor: A03
An MDC may not carry passengers and may not be ridden on an interstate highway or a sidewalk. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec03-F29 | anchor: A04
A for-hire endorsement covers hauling property for hire in a vehicle registered at 16,000 to 26,000 pounds gross weight, or carrying passengers for hire in a vehicle designed for fewer than 16 people including the driver. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec03-F30 | anchor: A04
A for-hire endorsement does not permit driving a commercial motor vehicle, and a CDL holder who wants to work as a limo, cab or ride share driver must pass the for-hire exam and add the endorsement. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec03-F31 | anchor: A04
A for-hire endorsement requires age 18 and at least one year holding a valid Indiana license; a new applicant passes both the driver and for-hire knowledge exams, while a current unexpired license holder takes only the for-hire exam. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec03-F32 | anchor: A04
A license carrying a for-hire endorsement can be renewed at a branch or online up to one year before it expires. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec03-F33 | anchor: A04
The BMV does not require a medical examination report for the for-hire endorsement; drivers unsure whether their vehicle needs one should contact the Indiana Department of Transportation. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec03-F34 | anchor: A04
Driving a medical services vehicle, or hauling property for hire in a vehicle registered under 16,000 pounds, does not count as transporting for hire. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0021]

Misconceptions: an autocycle needs no motorcycle endorsement even though it has three wheels; letter B means glasses on a license restriction but motor driven cycle on an ID card endorsement; a for-hire endorsement never authorizes a commercial motor vehicle; a valid permit or license already covers motor driven cycle riding without an MDC endorsement.
Mnemonics: B for bifocals (glasses or contacts), F for field-of-view aids (mirrors or camera), G for go by daylight; MDC means fifteen, fifty cc and thirty-five tops.
Glossary: restriction means a condition the holder must meet while driving; endorsement means an added privilege such as motorcycle or for-hire; autocycle means an enclosed three-wheeler driven with a wheel and pedals; motor driven cycle means a registered small-engine cycle of no more than fifty cubic centimeters; Ride Safe Indiana means the state's approved motorcycle training program.
Dynamic facts: endorsement fees, Ride Safe Indiana provider lists, the RideSafeIndiana.com and IN.gov/BMV pages and renewal channels can change; confirm them on IN.gov/BMV.

corpus_stability.reason: The Indiana Driver's Manual back cover reads Published July 2026 and tells readers to check IN.gov/BMV for updates; the BMV manual page says printed manuals are updated at most once a year, so the selected pages are treated as stable within a year while fees and service details stay dynamic.
